source_refs.note: Topic printed 5.3.1.1 Handling Missing Data (PDF 134-135, printed 131-132); the number 5.3.1.1 is repeated inside 5.3.3. The book fills Sara's grade with 75 in Table 5.2 but imputes 82 here. Recorded.

blocks.text: Some data are incomplete. If only a few rows have missing values they can be removed; otherwise missing values can be filled with an average or with data from similar cases. The choice depends on the kind of data and how much is missing. If Sara's grade is missing:

items: Imputation: estimate the value from existing data, for example give her the class average of 82 for now, keeping the data set complete under a reasonable assumption.
Flagging: add a note that her grade is unavailable, so analysts know the data are incomplete; this is transparent and the analysis can continue.
Removal: if few entries are missing, leave her record out of certain analyses; this is acceptable if it does not distort the overall picture, but it loses information about Sara.
